title: Prospective Routine Investigation of Monocytic HLA-DR Expression in Clinical Applications
summary:
mHLA-DR – A MARKER OF IMMUNE FUNCTION: mHLA-DR (monocytic Human Leukocyte Antigen – DR) is a cell surface protein belonging to the MHC class II molecule family. It is expressed on antigen-presenting cells, particularly on monocytes. The function of MHC class II molecules involves the presentation of peptide antigens to CD4-positive T lymphocytes.

MEASUREMENT METHODOLOGY: Quantification of mHLA-DR expression is routinely performed using flow cytometry. Results are typically reported as the number of antibody binding sites per cell (AB/C) or as the percentage of HLA-DR-positive monocytes. Standardized measurement protocols are available.

PHYSIOLOGICAL CONTEXT: mHLA-DR expression is subject to dynamic regulation. Various endogenous and exogenous factors can influence expression density. mHLA-DR expression is considered a parameter of monocyte activation.

CURRENT STATUS: The determination of mHLA-DR expression is an established laboratory diagnostic method. It is employed in various clinical and scientific contexts. Interpretation of measured values is performed with consideration of the respective clinical question.
conditions: The primary aim of this prospective observational study is to investigate mHLA-DR in a hospital cohort and to integrate mHLA-DR status into routine blood count analysis.

Exclusion criteria:
